---
title: "Maintenance, Governance and Succession Patterns"
description: "Practical patterns for keeping evidence, code and responsibility transferable"
---

## Assign ownership before release

Open source permits reuse; it does not supply a maintainer. A survey of 104 deprecated projects associated failure with several technical and social conditions; a study of 352 SourceForge projects associated governance practices with maintenance. Neither establishes a causal survival intervention for type 1 diabetes (T1D) games ([Coelho and Valente, 2017](https://doi.org/10.1145/3106237.3106246); [Midha and Bhattacherjee, 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dss.2012.03.002)).

The following is a **proposed operational checklist**, informed by research-software guidance—not a validated T1D-game sustainability score.

| Responsibility | Required handover material |
|---|---|
| Product ownership | Named decision-maker, intended audience, scope and funding responsibilities |
| Software and release | Repository, reproducible build, dependency versions, account-transfer procedure and release instructions |
| Clinical and educational content | Sources, claims, review dates, known limitations and designated reviewers |
| Design and accessibility | Learning objectives, scenario rationale, user findings and accessibility tests |
| Evidence and data | Tested releases, protocols, assessments, consent and data-retention responsibilities |
| Distribution and succession | Hosting and store ownership, support route, successor and retirement conditions |

An owner may cover several roles, but a role should not exist only as tacit knowledge.

## Make the project reconstructible

Keep the scientific knowledge, physiological model where relevant, game rules and presentation separable. Store scenarios, text and translations in inspectable formats. This reduces the amount a new contributor must understand to correct one kind of error; it is an architectural proposal, not demonstrated educational benefit.

Research-software guidance recommends version control, documented installation, modularity and automated tests ([Taschuk and Wilson, 2017](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005412); [Fritz et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.14279/eceasst.v83.2622)). A release package should identify its licence, dependencies, exact source version, build command, test command, deployment route and known limitations. Record why non-obvious design or model choices were made.

The **Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable principles for research software (FAIR4RS)** support persistent identification, metadata and explicit reuse conditions; “accessible” does not require every resource to be unrestricted ([Chue Hong et al., 2022](https://doi.org/10.15497/RDA00068)). Software citation principles support attribution to a specific version rather than an undated homepage ([Smith et al., 2016](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.86)).

## Test what successors could accidentally break

| Change | Minimum relevant check |
|---|---|
| Scientific text | Citation supports the revised claim; uncertainty and intended population remain explicit |
| Physiological model | Units, conservation, isolated mechanisms, reference scenarios and edge cases |
| Learning rules | A valid strategy still achieves the stated objective; scoring does not reward a known misconception |
| Interface | Start, action, feedback, help, pause and exit work on supported inputs |
| Translation | Meaning, terminology, layout and links remain consistent with the source version |
| Dependency or deployment | Build from a clean checkout; verify distribution, offline claims and external services |

The [model-family chapter](../physiology/model-families.qmd) specifies model validation; [human factors](../human-factors/onboarding-and-accessibility.qmd) specifies user tasks. Automated checks do not replace content review or testing with intended users.

Keep dependencies proportionate to the task. For each external service, record what stops working if it disappears, who controls access and whether an offline or replaceable alternative exists. A dependency lockfile preserves a version selection, not the future availability of the service.

## Support contribution and succession

Provide small, reproducible issues, contribution instructions, test expectations and a named review route. Credit maintenance, clinical review, translations and documentation alongside new features; research-software sustainability work argues for recognising these contributions ([Druskat et al., 2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.06681)).

Test a handover: can someone other than the original author build the project, explain one design decision, correct a defect and prepare a release using only its records? Document the missing steps. Do not treat a public repository as proof that this exercise is possible.

## Artificial intelligence: test the contribution

**Artificial intelligence (AI)** assistants may help explain code, draft tests or find inconsistencies, but productivity and maintainability effects are context-dependent. A two-phase study with 151 participants found no clear downstream maintainability advantage or disadvantage when new developers modified AI-assisted code ([Borg et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-026-10889-1)). A randomised study of 16 experienced open-source developers completing 246 tasks in familiar repositories found that early-2025 tools increased completion time by 19%; this preprint does not establish the effect of later tools or other developer populations ([Becker et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09089)).

Proposed safeguards are to keep changes reviewable, require relevant before/after tests, verify scientific references independently and retain human responsibility for clinical claims and releases. Do not submit private health data or credentials to an assistant without appropriate authorisation and governance. Generated explanations are useful handover material only after someone checks them against the actual code.

## Retire explicitly when maintenance ends

Publish the final supported version, end-of-support date, known failures and status of hosted services. Preserve licensed source, documentation and the version used in research; handle accounts and data according to the applicable commitments. Distinguish an archived research artifact from a currently supported intervention, and remove acquisition claims that no longer hold.
